# heading-style

- ID: `MD003`
- Category: Headings
- Default: on, severity warning
- Fixable: yes
- Tags: `headings`

Headings all use the first heading's style: \# Title, \# Title \#, or
underlined.

## Why

One heading style makes the source easier to read and to search.

## Options

Set them under `rules.heading-style.options`.

- `style` (`string`, default `consistent`): Heading syntax to require.
  consistent takes the syntax of the first heading. Values: `consistent`, `atx`,
  `atx_closed`, `setext`, `setext_with_atx`, `setext_with_atx_closed`.
- `require_closing_atx` (`boolean`, default `false`, gomdlint only): Expect
  closed headings, such as \# Title \#, wherever the style expects ATX headings.

## Fix

The fix converts headings between the \# Title and \# Title \# styles. gomdlint
reports an underlined heading, or one that needs an underline, without a fix.
gomdlint may report a finding without a fix when the fix would change a line
with one character in brackets, such as \[x\] or \[1\], or the lines around it
up to a blank line, because it could add or remove a task list checkbox.

## Example

This document breaks the rule:

```markdown
# Guide

## Install ##

Run the installer.
```

gomdlint reports:

```text
3:1 Heading style 'atx_closed' does not match expected style 'atx'
```

The fix changes it to:

```markdown
# Guide

## Install

Run the installer.
```

## Configure

```yaml
rules:
  heading-style:
    options:
      style: consistent
```

Under `rules`, `heading-style: false` turns the rule off and
`heading-style: error` reports its findings as errors. The flag
`--disable heading-style` turns it off for one run.

## Silence one line

```markdown
<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line heading-style -->
```
